$comment: Native realtime session opening plan (context pipeline contract §3.1). Every client feeds `input` (assemble.v1 input shape plus contextWindow from the voice catalog realtime[] entry) to its production ContextPlan with purpose realtimeSession and compares the PlannedRealtimeSession projection with `expected` (strings byte-exact). History inputs are sanitize-identity (all delivered, user first, alternating); sanitize itself is locked by sanitize.v1.

constants.deliveryRealtime: The user is talking with you by voice in real time and hears your spoken replies. Speak naturally in short sentences, usually under 80 words unless the user asks for detail. Do not read out Markdown, code, tables, lists, or emoji; say symbols and units in words. Reply in the language the user is speaking unless the conversation instructions say otherwise.

rules: B = contextWindow (integer >= 1, else reject unknown_window). limit = floor(B/2). systemMax = min(floor(0.25*B), systemMaxCap). est text = ceil(utf8Bytes * rhoHi) (rhoHi defaults to rho0); est message = est text + messageOverheadTokens (budget.v1).

system = assemble.v1 layout 0-4 and 11 with B as above: skill, instructions, standingInstructions, memory, notes, knowledge; never toolSafety (realtime has no tools). Shrink while est message(system) > systemMax: last knowledge file, then last note, then last unpinned memory fact. knowledge is the skill’s attached knowledge files as given in input; the host never runs per-message knowledge retrieval (vector search on the latest user text) for a realtime plan, neither when opening nor when replanning at a turn boundary, so the session’s own transcripts cannot change instructions.

history = each input message projected to text: the message text, then one placeholder line per attachment in attachment order (constants.attachmentPlaceholders by kind; unknown kind = file), joined by \n; messages whose projected text is empty are skipped; after skipping, leading assistant messages are skipped too (the session always starts with user). Roles stay user / assistant.

checkpoint (non-empty string) = prefix checkpoint + \n\n on the first user message of the kept history; when the kept history has no user message it is its own first item {role user, text checkpoint} with id null. The checkpoint is never dropped.

[D] = non-empty parts joined by 

: <oriveo-reminder> (same rule as assemble.v1 layout 8 with B: conversation instructions non-empty and (user messages in history >= reminderMinUserMessages or est message(system) + est messages(history incl. checkpoint) >= floor(0.30*B)); reminderEnabled false → no reminder; user messages are counted in the input history before projection; body xml(trim(instructions)) when est text(trim(instructions)) — unescaped — <= reminderFullTextMaxTokens else reminderPointer), then <oriveo-delivery>
{deliveryRealtime}
</oriveo-delivery> (always). instructions = system + 

 + [D], or [D] alone when system is null.

Budget: estimatedInjected = est message(instructions) + sum est message(history item). If est message(instructions), plus the checkpoint item when there is one, > limit → reject instructions_too_long (instructions, history and fingerprint null). Otherwise drop history from the oldest by whole messages until estimatedInjected <= limit; after a drop the kept history always starts at a user message (an assistant left first is dropped too).

fingerprint = {instructionsSha256: lowercase hex sha256 of the UTF-8 instructions, lastHistoryId: id of the last kept history item, null when none}. A turn boundary with a different fingerprint (either field) closes the session and opens a new one from the new plan; a Gemini resumption handle is only used within one fingerprint. While a session is open the host replans with currentSessionId = that session: history messages persisted from it (realtimeSessionId equal) are left out of the plan, so the session’s own transcripts never reopen it; a new session is planned with currentSessionId null and reads them as ordinary history.
omitted.history = input messages with non-empty projected text that were dropped by the budget. memoryIds as assemble.v1 layout 16.
